utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone. Mark Harmon and Carmela Javier appearing for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Harmon. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon to everyone, Daniela Tasic, Chad Mair, Milos Androvic, Eric Tully, Tina Drolec, Novak Lukic, and I'm Gregor Guy-Smith, appearing on behalf of Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. If the record may show that we're still sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis in the absence of Judge David for the same reasons as yesterday. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Before I begin the examination of Mr. Butler, a point came up yesterday in respect of helicopter flights. That issue has never been part of our case, but it has become an issue apparently in this case, and so I have and will be disclosing to the Defence today a number of reports relating to that subject area, and I will present to Your Honours evidence relating to that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. And if you don't mind, may I interrupt you. There's something I forgot to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Butler. I have to remind you, sir, that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, yesterday in the course of these proceedings we saw a film-clip with General Krstic in Potocari with buses and trucks operating behind him. In chapter 5 of Prosecution Exhibit 2246, you deal with the subject of movement of Muslims from the former Srebrenica enclave, and in particular, Mr. Butler, in chapter -- in paragraph 5.6, you say: "Further on, 12 July 1995, General-Major Krstic was active in organising and directing the transportation of the Muslim civilian population." What I'd like to do, Mr. Butler, is I'd like to show you a number of documents, and I would like you -- like to invite your comments on them. If we could have, first of all, 65 ter 2591.02 on the screen. First of all let me identify the document, Mr. Butler. It's in small print in front of you on the monitor. This is a document, and that is dated the 12th of July, 1995. It is a regular combat report from the command of the 1st Zvornik Brigade, and it is addressed to the command of the Drina Corps. And if we could go to the second page in both the English and the B/C/S. We can see that the author of this document is Lieutenant-Colonel Vinko Pandurevic who we have seen earlier in film footage in yesterday's evidence. What I'd like to do, Mr. Butler, is direct your attention -- if we could go back to the first page. I would like to direct your attention to paragraph 2. That portion in the middle of the paragraph, a little bit below the middle of the paragraph that says: "We sent to Bratunac pursuant to your order eight buses from Drinatrans, two buses from our VP, and four of our trucks." First of all, this reference is pursuant to "your order." Whose order is being referred to by Colonel Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, in this context, the order that they're referring to, "your order," would be their higher command, the headquarters of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And how does -- based on your analysis of the documents and the evidence, how does this paragraph that I have just -- a portion of this paragraph that I've read to you relate to the movement of the population from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, if you go back and following the context of the second meeting at the Hotel Fontana, following that second meeting and then through the evening there are a series of orders that are published by both the Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence and also the military commands to include the Drina Corps out to various military units, out to various civilian governmental-owned enterprises to start assembling buses and have them go to Bratunac. In this particular case, what you have is the Zvornik Brigade command responding back that pursuant to the Drina Corps order to send vehicles down to Bratunac that they have complied with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Could we focus on the next sentence which reads: "One military police detachment was sent to Konjevic Polje pursuant to your order." Now, Mr. Butler -- first of all, what does this sentence mean in light of the documents that you have read and reviewed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had requested, they being the Drina Corps, had requested that a military police patrol go to the Konjevic Polje intersection where they would participate in traffic control knowing that that was going to be the route that the buses were going to be going down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the route that buses were going to be going down, tell me where the buses were going and would they be going through this particular town, Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The buses for the women and the children originated in Potocari, went through Bratunac, then along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, at the intersection of Konjevic Polje, they turned towards the westerly direction through Milici, Vlasenica, up into a town known as Tisca. And at that point the buses stopped. The individuals disembarked the buses and then walked through a tunnel, that tunnel being an area connecting the territory under the control of the Republika Srpska and the territory under the control of the, at that time, the Bosnian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2394.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have next on the monitor Prosecution Exhibit 280. For reference, this also is found in the same report at footnote 245.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, this is an intercepted conversation at 915 hours. Can you date this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe that the investigation and the individuals who created this date it as 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And can you identify who Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic is and what his position was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic was the chief of transportation services for the command of the Drina Corps on -- in July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, can you just comment on this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's a summary of an actual conversation, and they're discussing the fact that -- one of the correspondents is replying that without the proper authorisation, one, they only have two buses, and two, that they can't move them without the proper authorisation that has to be written. And the third problem that you see discussed here is the lack of fuel, both within the Republika Srpska and in other areas. So one of the critical issues that this entire movement of the civilian population were going to hinge on was getting the available fuel for the vehicles that needed to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might just ask, is the typewritten portion that's in English a complete summary of that whole page that's handwritten?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are you asking me, Your Honour? Or, Mr. Butler, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm asking Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, it is not. The conversation that you see in B/C/S below that is a different conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And from the page in B/C/S, what is the English version a summary of? Is it the summary of the first paragraph, middle paragraph, or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it's the summary of the middle paragraph, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I note the name Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic in that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness kindly push his microphones apart. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have Prosecution Exhibit 261 on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, this is a conversation between two participants unidentified, X and Y. First of all, can you date this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe this intercept has been dated 12 July 1995, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And can you comment on this intercept and what relationship this intercept had with the movement of the civilian population from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first component of the intercept gives a rundown of where vehicles are being collected from and coming from. The next portion of that talks about where they still believe vehicles will be in-bound from. They're talking about the empty tanker truck coming in as well as a request for fuel has been forwarded to Krstic, and that so far over 50 buses have been obtained.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Could we turn to the next exhibit, which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I'm may, I'm not understanding the correlation between the English translation and that which is on the screen in B/C/S to be perfectly honest with you. It seems to be a great deal more information and different kind of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can direct counsel and Your Honours. It's the middle conversation. There is a series of numbers on the left-hand side that say 2535. So for counsel's benefit and Your Honours' benefit, this longer document in B/C/S on the right contains other conversations or portions of other conversations. And the conversation that is P261 is the portion of the conversation in the middle that starts at 785.00 megahertz and ends with, at the lower right-hand side, the initials FAFA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much, and I would appreciate it to the extent that there should be a one-to-one correlation between the English and the B/C/S. If we could have that remedied at some point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess that goes for the previous exhibit as well, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We'll take care of that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have -- could I have the next exhibit which is Prosecution Exhibit 260 on the screen. This is also referred to in footnote 245. And for the benefit of counsel and the Court, the very short intercept in English on the left is -- the intercept again that starts on the fourth line down 785.000 and ends -- it's three lines long. And we will, obviously, address the concerns of the Court and counsel in respect of isolating that intercept from the remainder of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, first of all, please examine the intercept that I'm referring to. It's in English. And can you inform us, first of all, of the date of this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This intercept has been dated 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Again, if I might ask, how do you determine that, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, the -- as a component of previous trials, many of the intercept operators who have taken these has -- have testified behind them, as well as the Office of the Prosecutor has engaged in a rather exhaustive effort with all of these intercepts to both authenticate them and date them where they fall in context of other things. For example, if you look at the right-hand document, that's part of a larger book. And when you look at that larger book in total, you'll find there will be notations to the days that they're doing it. They will only date it once and then put the time hatch down on subsequent conversations. So because of that prior analytical work that was done by the Office of the Prosecutor that is how I can date this to 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That leaves me with some cold comfort, Your Honour, in terms of the kinds of evidence that's being presented to this Chamber at this time. It seems to me there should be some correlation between the specific document. And apparently there is some written documentation that would establish, assuming that what the gentleman said is accurate and I have no reason to disbelieve him at least for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So sorry. I know I'm wearing my earphones, but I'm losing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My voice is dropping, and I do apologise. I said that assuming that what the gentleman said is accurate, and I have no reason to disbelieve him for the moment, there is some written information there has memorialised that would establish that which he has said. And I am left with some, at this juncture, cold comfort in terms of his explanation because it doesn't have an evidential basis, and by that I mean there's a lack of foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, there's the cold comfort in which I find myself too. I was going to ask Mr. Butler that I do appreciate what he says, but I thought what the nub of your answer is that on this larger document which is handwritten, somewhere before this entry is made a date is given somewhere.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you happen to know that date to be the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, these -- before they were incorporated in my report, I am aware that that project there where we dated this material. So it certainly -- to my satisfaction, I know it's 12 July, otherwise I would not have incorporated it into my material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah. That's the nub of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: These notebooks were disclosed to the Defence, Your Honour, so the Defence has them and can examine them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, again, can you comment on this specifically in relation to how this relates to the movement of the civilian population from the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, it's just generally a one-line that reflects first but the two correspondents Krstic being General Krstic, and Krsmanovic being Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic, and the notation that Krstic wants the buses to start moving right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And to put this in context, Mr. Butler, when this is at 1210 hours, when did the last of the Hotel Fontana meetings end on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the time that everyone coalesces around is 11.30 is when the last of the meetings ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. If we could turn to Prosecution Exhibit 262, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is referred to, Your Honours, in footnote 247 of Mr. Butler's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, first of all, can you date this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is also 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And can you comment on this and how it relates to the movement of the civilian population from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can. The first part of the conversation, I mean -- and just to set the stage, the individual listed as Sobot is in fact Major Sobot, who is the chief of technical services for the Drina Corps on this day in July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it not a she manning the switchboard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, where it says Krstic and Sobot ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. Because somewhere Krstic says "put me back to the switchboard."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- or to the switchboard --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Miss, put me through." He says, "Miss, put me through."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is he not speaking to a lady?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He may be speaking to a lady whose monitoring a conversation, but Sobot is in fact the chief of the technical services; it's not the switchboard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first part of the conversation occurs at the headquarters of the Drina Corps where Krstic is calling in to the Drina Corps. Sobot is there at that time and they're discussing the buses and others to make the road secure. At that time if you've noticed, sir, General Krstic goes back and says, Put me through to the switchboard, to the Vlasenica brigade. They switch him through there, and now he's talking to Major Kosoric. This is a different Kosoric than the chief of the intelligence service. This is, I believe, is the chief of staff of the Vlasenica Brigade. And Krstic is discussing the issues relating to securing the road and getting in touch with the police to ensure that the road is secure all the way up to the tunnel area which is -- will be the ultimate debarkation point of the individuals in the buses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, if we can, I'd like to turn our attention to Potocari once again, and on the 12th or 13th of July. And in your report, paragraphs 5.22 and 5.23, you refer to buses being loaded in Bratunac Brigade, persons and VRS military police manning the separation lines and guarding access to the buses. So if we could look at 65 ter 4559P, some film footage. We'll stop this again like we did yesterday, Mr. Butler, and I'm going to be asking you some questions to identify certain units, people. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, you'll see as this film progresses, and we've passed a couple soldiers already, are you able to identify, first of all, the units from which those soldiers come?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The ongoing investigation has identified them as members of the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, there is a gentleman, a soldier in the right-hand side of this image. He has -- looks to be wearing a tri-coloured band on his left bicep. Can you identify which unit that individual's from?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's the Bratunac Brigade Military Police Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. And just for the record, Your Honour, we've stopped this at 2.13.09.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And can you -- was the Bratunac Brigade military platoon a subordinate of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The police platoon belonged to the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, that, in turn, was a subordinate formation of the Drina Corps, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll continue with this film for just a ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could this be given an Exhibit Number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's so given. May it please be given number, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P2395.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, Mr. Butler, we saw some film footage with a number of high-ranking members of the Drina Corps in and around Potocari when the buses were moving to and fro. Was General Mladic in the area near the buses at the time that Bosnian Muslim civilians were boarding those buses?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have -- could we play 65 ter 4559Q, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have stopped at 03.03.48.7 and who is the man it he short-sleeved short and the camouflage uniform in the middle of this image?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That sir is General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And do you know where that image, Mr. Butler, was taken?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That image was taken in Potocari, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could that be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given an exhibit number, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P2396, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now I want to refer you, Mr. Butler, in your report to paragraphs 5.24 to 5.26. This deals with Tisca and Luke. And could you very, very briefly --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My apologies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I just want to make sure. Which report are we on now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, can you just briefly describe what happened at that location and let me ask you some additional questions before we look at a film clip.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. At that location is where the buses ended their journey. The people got off the buses. There was one final separation that occurred there. If for whatever reason there were any military-aged males or other people that they wanted to separate, they would do them there and they put them in a nearby school. It's called the school at Luke. The women and children and the elderly then went to Muslim-held territory, and those individuals who had been detained were taken -- were in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What happened to the individuals in the school, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that according to the one survivor that on the evening 13th July, they were taken out to a remote location and executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Could we have 65 ter 4559R on the screen. Before we -- before we actually look at this image, Mr. Butler, these film clips, were you able to identify the units of the VRS that were present at Tisca and Luke?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the units would be members of the Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade and the Milici Light Infantry Brigade, both of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. If we could play this image, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could this be given an exhibit number, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It will be -- let me just ask one or two questions. Mr. Butler, I seem to observe what looked like women, children, and very old men. I didn't see the separation of the men from the women as you indicated, or is this not the point where that happens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, and you will not see that on the video footage, as far as I'm aware. There's no video footage of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The clip is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P2397, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the image that we just saw, Mr. Butler, was the image of people getting off buses and walking in a direction. In what direction were they walking?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were walking towards Bosnian Muslim-held territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. If we could take a look at 65 ter 4559S which relates to this period of time. This is the Luke-Kladanj road, 12 or 13 July 1995. If we could play that, please. We'll stop this, Mr. Butler, at some points in the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, what does this film depict, first of all?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This film depicts the beginning of the group of individuals arriving into Bosnian Muslim-held territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In the an image - and we've stopped this at 02:15:45:4 - there are -- there's an individual with a blue cap in the middle of the image, and to the left -- to his right, I'm sorry, there's a tall soldier in a camouflage T-shirt, camouflage pants. Could you identify that individual who is in camouflage T-shirt and pants? He's the second person in the foreground from the left.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe that's imagine Boering from the Dutch Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We've seen Major Boering earlier in previous film footage?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he was at the Hotel Fontana meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And he appears to be accompanying, and in fact is accompanying this group of Bosnian Muslims who have been let off the buses and are walking towards the Muslim territory. Can you comment on his presence and whether the presence of UN personnel in the buses was common?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. One of the things that -- and I have believe Colonel Karremans even noted in his discussions was that one of the things that the UN wanted to do was to escort these convoys out to ensure their safety. At the beginning of the movement of the population out, they put either Dutch personnel in some of the buses or in vehicles accompanying the convoys. That worked for the first couple of convoys, but what rapidly began to happen and as the Dutch started to realise that at various points along the convoy route either Serb soldiers, the Bosnian Serb soldiers, or the Republika Srpska police would be stopping the Dutch, confiscating their vehicles and weapons, and holding them at other locations. So as time goes by as part of this movement, the ability of the Dutch UN soldiers to monitor the movement is degraded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not following you very well. You started off by saying the Dutch personnel would be in the buses. But now you are saying they would stop their vehicles, confiscate their weapons. Are they in the vehicles, or are they in the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It started as both. In some cases the Dutch soldiers were riding in the buses. For most part, they used their own vehicles. And what happened in both cases was that the Bosnian Serb military and police units there as the Dutch would go by would be to confiscate the Dutch UN vehicles and the weapons of the all of the soldiers. And by, of course, doing that, it would degrade their ability to monitor that and return back to the Dutch Battalion headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And did you -- who did you say here is -- is the Dutch -- well, is it the man in the blue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir. The man in the middle to the left of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The man in the middle, okay. And the one in the blue headgear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know his identity, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can't even identify the uniform which he comes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would assume from the blue beret that he is a UN member, but I don't know any of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm trying to keep away from calling it a blue helmet, that's why I say blue gear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a beret; it's not a helmet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know what it is. I cannot say. Is it a beret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It appears to be a beret, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just before we move off of that, if we just get some information, if the gentleman has any, on the third person in camouflage unit so we don't have to return to it at a later point in time, if he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are you able to assist us, Mr. Butler, in identifying either the unit or the person who is at the far left of this particular image? He's wearing -- it looks like a white belt.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The white belt is typical of a military police individual. However, I cannot tell you whether or not that's somebody at the far end who is a Bosnian Muslim military police member or a member of the Bosnian Serb military police. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were the uniforms of the two police similar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost identical. Many of the combatants wore the former uniforms of the JNA. So uniform alone wouldn't necessarily be a discriminator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, are you able to identify at least the -- which army the individual is who is in -- about the middle of the screen, wearing a camouflage uniform and helping a woman in what appears to be a purplish colour garment. And just for the record, we're at 02:16:04:5?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe at this point in the video, it bounces back and forth. I believe at this point the individual is a member of the Bosnian Muslim military forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we just saw, Mr. Butler, the caption. It said the Tuzla aeroport. What role did the Tuzla aeroport play on the 12th or 13th of July, 1995, in these events?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Tuzla was the headquarters of the UN UNPROFOR Sector North east. I believe they were at the aeroport. And after these refugees came through the tunnel and were immediately met in Muslim territory, there was an effort to pick them up from where they were at the Kladanj area and then move them to a better staged facility for them at the Tuzla aeroport.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could this be given -- could this be given exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P2398, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, now I'd like to return to Potocari on the 13th of July, 1995, and specifically I'd like to refer you to your report, paragraphs 5.18 to 5.20 in the Prosecution Exhibit 2246. The subject matter being the separation of Muslim males in Potocari. I'm going to show you three -- two clips of video. First of all, if we could start with P387, and I'm only going to show you a portion of this video and ask you to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Actually, we can stop the video there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, let me show you two other portions of video, and then I'm going to invite your comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 4559T on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Butler, the portion of the film -- and we've stopped this at 02.25.38.8. The portion of the film that precedes that counter number, what does that depict?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, it depicts the separation, or not necessarily the process, but the result. As you can see in the video, the women, children, and elderly men are travelling down one side of the line of buses and trucks. There are soldiers, or at this point in time on the 13th, members of the Republika Srpska police in between each vehicle, and that the able-bodied men are going down the other side, and they're not letting the two groups mingle.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what did the interior of that bus depict?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, I think it was all completely women. There may have been one or two children in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to view this film footage that starts at 2.25.38.8. And I'll just let you know that this is a very, very short portion of the film and advise Your Honours that this very, very short. It's a matter of seconds, this film.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just for purposes of clarification, and it maybe my older eyes, which is with regard to what this depicts, and that's all I'm referring to, are you indicating that both groups are depicted in this particular shot? That's what I'm trying to get to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In the shot that's now before us?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the shot that's now before us, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, if you just forebear for a moment and --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, the reason I ask the question is because you asked him a specific -- Mr. Harmon ask him a specific question with regard to this portion of the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, I asked the question about the film footage that preceded this counter number. So the film footage that started out, it had two separate portions of it. It had the men who were coming down the side of a bus, and then it went to the interior of a bus --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now we're focussed on this, and we're going to play this very short portion of the film. And I'm going to invite Mr. Butler to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I now understand what you've done.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. So if we could play this film, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. That was a -- Mr. Butler, we can replay that if you like and for the Court's benefit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'd like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you replay that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take it that Your Honour wanted to have me play the portion that lasted about five seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's so fast, Your Honour, that we'll play it -- if the Court or counsel wish, we'll play it one more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have -- I have one or two questions to ask. I saw soldiers in blue headgear. I just wanted to find out from Mr. Butler that whether the Dutch police or UNPROFOR -- beg your pardon, not police but soldiers, or UNPROFOR's people still with them here at this time when now it appears that men are being separated from the women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they are. And I believe you'll see some further film clips of that. The Dutch -- this is Potocari. This is the Dutch base, so they are still here. You'll also note that by this time that none of them armed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I noticed that. Will you know whether some of the UNPROFOR people accompanied the males wherever they had been taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only UN people who are allowed to accompany any males that left were the, I believe, 50 or so wounded men taken from the Dutch Battalion clinic area and were taken to the medical centre that had been set up in Bratunac. I believe one or two of the Dutch doctors were allowed to accompany them at least as early as the 13th and 14th. If I recall correctly, at some juncture the doctors were sent away. But for the separation process that you see here in Potocari and that these people later go to Bratunac, the Dutch were not permitted to accompany them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The able-bodied men, the unwounded men, the healthy men.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They were in the allowed to accompany them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could that 65 ter 4559T be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P2399, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have Prosecution Exhibit 389 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, before -- we're going to stop the film. And this is at 2.28.34.0. Can you identify the soldier in a camouflage uniform wearing a blue beret?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is Major Kingori. He is not a member of the Dutch Battalion, but he in fact is one of the United Nations' military observers who was at Srebrenica and later at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, do you know where the men who had been separated were taken in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The primary facility that they were taken to was a two- or three-storey building that we know as the white house. It was a building there that the men were being held in, and then later buses would come or trucks would come for them and they would take them to Bratunac. So that structure's known as the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you refer to that in your report, I believe, in paragraph 519, 519, of Prosecution Exhibit 2246.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the white house is in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have Prosecution Exhibit 3 -- P390 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We've stopped at film at 2:29:49:7. Mr. Butler, this is -- depicts a pile of some kind. Can you tell us what's -- that pile represents?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Those are the -- those piles are the personal belongings of the men who had been separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, you say -- [inaudible]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, say again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you saying that the men were not allowed to take their personal belongings with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it known what became of these personal belongings finally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that at some juncture, once they were rifled through by the various people there that they were assembled and burned. They were considered waste products at that point and potentially hazardous, so they were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We're going to play another portion of this film. This -- now we're going to play this portion in just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I want to ask you, Mr. Butler, how far was that pile of goods that the personal belongings of the men who had been separated from the white house?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe witnesses who have -- you know, the Dutch primarily, who have described it say that pile goes all the way back and around.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: But how many metres or feet?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Is it close to the white house? Is it a long way away from the white house?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's actually in very close proximity to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And did your review of the documents in this case establish the purpose, the ostensible purpose for putting men in the white house?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what was that purpose?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the context of the conflict that had been going on in that area for several years, one of the things that they wanted to do was to screen the Muslim men that were coming into their custody for their potential involvement in war crimes against the Serbs. And in fact the Bratunac Brigade, on the 12th of July, published a list of 400 individuals who, according to them, were involved in war crimes against local Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, Mr. Butler, were there any investigations conducted of Bosnian Muslim men who had been separated in Potocari for the commission of war crimes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, not in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were there ever any investigations conducted of Bosnian Muslim men from the Srebrenica enclave for the commission of war crimes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one individual that I'm aware of, sir, and it was one of the individuals who was among those 50 some-odd people who were evacuated to Bratunac with the Dutch. There will actually be a document, that I believe is dated either 17th or 18th July, that talks about the moment of those people under the control of the Bosnian Serb military and the ICRC with the exception of one individual who is going into police custody because he is somebody who is wanted for war crimes against the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And do you refer to that in paragraph 8.1 of Prosecution Exhibit 2246? The last sentence is that -- the reference point is? Page 79.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Butler, we have 2.30 -- we stopped at film at 2.30.18.9. And it says, "Studio B segment, Petrovic footage." Can you enlighten us as to Studio B and where it's located?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Studio B is a Belgrade-based production facility. Zoran Petrovic part of that. What we look at it when we refer to it from an investigative point of view of the Studio B segment, is that we are aware that the entire unaltered, for the most part, version of this was played over Belgrade television. And then once it was played over Belgrade television, the Office of the Prosecutor, through its channels back then, made a request for the video. We got from the authorities there a version of the video that had some edits in it. So when you see the moniker Studio B segment, what you're looking at is parts of the video that are not altered -- or not -- not that I should say altered, but these are some of the portions that did not initially come into the hands of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me put it a different way. Is this Studio B portion the unedited version of this film clip?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if we could play this, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay, I've stopped it at 2.30.40.5. Can you identify the building where there appears to be a balcony and men seated behind the balcony?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That is the facility that we refer to as the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, I want to change locations now both in terms of the geography of the Srebrenica area and in terms of the location in your report. Specifically I want to refer you to those portions of your report, paragraph 6.13 to paragraph 6.25 in Prosecution Exhibit 2246 where you describe the RS, MUP, and Drina Corps units on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road on the 12th and 13th of July, 1995. In that section you identify persons and units who were involved in the events along that part of the road. Can you locate us -- first of all, where is this road, the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road in relation to the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: A bit difficult without a map, but if I can try and draw a mental picture. The road runs parallel to the route that the Bosnian Muslim column would be taking towards Muslim-held territory. So geographically speaking, where the road runs from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje is important. The relevance for this particular segment of film is the fact that because of its proximity to where the column was coming across, thousands of individuals from that column on various days surrendered to Bosnian Serb military and police forces along that stretch of the road. And that is the relevance of that particular road stretch to the Srebrenica -- the larger Srebrenica crime base.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this question, Mr. Butler. Was it -- did your evidence show or did the evidence you analysed, including this film clip, show that along -- all along that road the Bosnian Serb forces attempted to interdict the column as it was making its way north toward Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I really would appreciate [Microphone not activated]. Especially on something --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There we go. I really would appreciate it if Mr. Harmon would not lead the witness, especially on something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That portion of what I led the witness on is described in detail in this report, so I'm relating to certain elements of this report so I can introduce the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you establish a nexus -- I seem to be having trouble with my microphone. It seems to be going on and off. Perhaps we could get at that taken care of during the break. If he establishes a nexus between the report and the question, I obviously have no difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler in paragraph -- along that road there was a location known as Sandici meadow, and you refer to that in paragraph 6.29. Briefly, what occurred at Sandici meadow? What was the importance of Sandici meadow in these events?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prisoners being captured along or surrendering to the VRS and Republika Srpska police forces along that portion of the road were collected and guarded in the Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's start, if we can, with 65 ter 4559U. If that could be placed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this says "On the road." We stopped it at 2.37.43.9. Just for clarity of the record, which road are we talking about here, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we could play this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I've stopped this almost immediately at 2.37.49.5.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, where is this footage taken?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is at the Sandici meadow, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We've stopped at 02.39.25.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, can we identify the unit in which these two soldiers are members of?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they are members of the Republika Srpska Special Police Brigade, specifically the 2nd Sekovici Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And they were under whose command?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were directly under the command of the police, Lieutenant-Colonel Borovcanin was the senior police officer there. They operated under the control of the military at this juncture, because both the police and military forces were responsible for this road area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to stop this in just a few more seconds, but if we could play on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, we've stopped the film at 2.39.55.9. Do you know where this film footage is located?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe that's Sandici again, just a different view of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And there are some people standing. Can you identify those people?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that in the course of the investigation there -- you can't tell obviously from the distance here, but they're members of either the 2nd Sekovici Detachment or members of the 1st Municipal Police Company, the 1st PJP, that was also accompanying the 2nd Sekovici Detachment. So these are police personnel in this group. I don't believe any of them are soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, we're way --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I wasn't attentive to the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I wasn't either. I'm sorry. Is it convenient or would you finish -- mind if we finish?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We can carry on with this portion of the film after the recess, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about the late start. It was due to circumstances beyond our control. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can interrupt the playing of this film. What I have done is I have taken from the map book 65 ter 9243, which is a map, 15 of the map book. And I have printed hard copies for counsel, for the witness, and for Your Honours. If they could be distributed. They may be of -- oh, if Your Honours have the map books with you, then if I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Her Honour does; I didn't. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if the witness could be given a copy of this map, and if he can then, I think, provide greater clarity to the Court as to the locations that we have been talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, any comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I figured based on some of the questions that were being asked, it made sense for the map to be shown so that there was an understanding of what was being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, you have a hard copy of the map in front of you, and I want you to orient us, if you will, to this map. First of all, to the lower right-hand corner with a -- in a purplish line, it looks like an amoeba, can you identify what that purple line represents?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That is the boundary of the Srebrenica safe area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And within that purple line we can see both the town of Srebrenica, the town of Potocari. And to the left we can see two towns, Susnjari and Jaglici. Once again, can you just tell us the significance of Susnjari and Jaglici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was where the column of military-age Muslim men from Srebrenica assembled to begin to make their trek towards the free territory around Tuzla and Nezuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, from the town of Susnjari and Jaglici there appears to be red lines, two parallel red lines heading in a north-westerly direction, ending past a tunnel at the top, past Hadzici and Orahovac. Do you know what those red lines are?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. These red lines, their origin comes from a map that was seized by the Office of the Prosecutor from the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. It's a representation off of that Bosnian Serb military map in gross terms of the route of the column as it went from the former Srebrenica safe area to and through the lines of the Bratunac Brigade, the RS police, and then the rear area of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we again look at this map and we go from the town of Potocari and we go slightly up the road, we see the town of Bratunac. Can you just direct the Court's attention to the road between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje and the various locations on it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. From Bratunac, travelling in a left-hand direction on the map, you'll go through Glogova, Kravica, Sandici, and then up to the road intersection; it's known as the intersection between the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road. The actual village of Konjevic Polje is right around at that intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if we turn left on that road and descend, we go -- we go past Nova Kasaba; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just -- if the record could that when you say moving from Bratunac to the left, you mean in a north-westerly direction, slightly north but mainly west.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct, in that north-western direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, can you orient us from the intersection of Konjevic Polje to Tisca and Luke, the route that was taken with the people who had been forcibly transferred from the enclave. Could you just orient us on this map, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. As you follow that road, it goes south from Konjevic Polje to Nova Kasaba to Milici, west from Milici to Vlasenica, up into that north-westerly direction from Vlasenica to Tisca, and then west to Luke. And then of course that purple line that you see depicted on the map is -- at that time was the confrontation line, and that is where, you know -- separated the territory held under the control of the Republika Srpska and the territory under the control of the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now let me orient you to two features we've been talking about, and we will be seeing -- and we have just seen in this video-clip that we have been looking before we took a break, the Sandici meadows. Now, on this map between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje, there is a mark, Sandici. Is that -- does that represent the meadows or a village? What does that represent, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, sir, represents the meadow at Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. In your report, Mr. Butler, you identify a number of primary execution sites. Can you just -- are -- well, I see that they're marked in red with a red dot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And I see one location which -- Cerska is referred to in your report as the location of a mass execution. Did the mass execution take place in the town of Cerska, or did it take place at one of those dots on the road between Konjevic Polje and Cerska?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The execution, sir, did it not take place in the town; it took place along the river valley leading -- it's -- that area is known as the Cerska Valley. That actual execution took place in the valley area, not inside the actual town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. I think we'll refer to this map as we go along. And if the Court has any questions at this point in terms of features on this map, Your Honour, I invite you to -- could this be given an exhibit number then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2400.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, now what I'd like to do is return to the film clip that we were looking after before the break, and we start at -- we're going to start where we left off, which is 2.39.55.9, and if we could just carry on playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we stop there just for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Butler, we are stopped at 2.40.16.6. A second or two before it said "Studio B segment." Again, what does that mean in this -- in relation to the film we're about to watch?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the unedited portion of the film, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this -- you can see in the upper right-hand corner of this image where I have stopped the film, a logo. Can you tell us what that logo is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that is the Studio B logo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. If we can -- let me ask you one additional question. Can you identify the -- the soldiers and what unit they belong to, the one on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this shot pans around. Several of the soldiers are from the 2nd Sekovici. I can't tell you if the dog unit that we're looking at is from that particular unit as well, but they are Republika Srpska police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Then we can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I note that the man on the left in the picture seems to be in civilian clothes, or am I right? Am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, that as we play this, it will become clearer. I hope so, at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I don't think it did become clearer, Your Honour, so I -- but I think if we start again, we'll see a better image. If we could just -- Carmela, go back a little bit on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We stopped at -- we've stopped at 2.40.14.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, are you able to assist us with that image?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, it's a member of the RS police. It's not a civilian per se.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. But how do you know that if he's -- if he's in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I don't believe he's in civilian clothes. His top, he's wearing a police top, and it's my understanding from the investigation that all of these individuals have been identified as members of the RS police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We've stopped the film at 2.50.17.5.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, first of all, can you identify the man who is to the immediate right of the individual wearing the blue helmet?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Ljubisa Borovcanin, he's the deputy commander of the Republika Srpska Special Police Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And he is talking -- appears to be talking to somebody or at least facing in the direction of somebody wearing a blue helmet. What observations do you have about this frame of the footage?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I can tell you that that is not a United Nations individual. In fact, it's another member of the RS police. The Dutch, as part of their story, they talk about their weapons and their blue helmets and other things being stolen from them during the course of the days. Several of these survivors of the executions who ultimately were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor, talk about being -- or being coerced to surrender or being asked to surrender by individuals who were wearing United Nations gear. And in one case one particular individual says that, you know, up until the time that he surrendered he thought he was putting himself in the custody of the United Nations, only to realise that in fact it wasn't. So this is not an uncommon theme that you will have these individuals wearing UN equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We've stopped the film at 2.52.00.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, the young boy in the purple sweater who appears in this image, what was his fate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He actually survived, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And has he been a witness in this institution, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could 65 ter 4559U be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2401.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, I want to turn to your report, if I could, P2246. I want to turn to paragraphs 6.28 to 6.31, and then also to -- through to 6.36. Those portions, Mr. Butler, you discuss the Kravica warehouse events, the massacre on the 13th of July, 1995. We have a map before us that show the location of Kravica and Sandici. My question to you is what is the relationship between the prisoners who were detained at the Sandici meadow, we've seen them in the video earlier, and the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the prisoners who were held in the Sandici meadow, captured, and then brought there throughout the course of the day, were either taken by buses and trucks or were marched down the road by foot to the Kravica warehouse. So almost everyone who was at the Sandici meadow prior to about 1600 or so ultimately went to the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the units that were responsible for transporting the prisoners from the Sandici meadow to Kravica warehouse and the persons responsible for guarding them, which units did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They belonged to the Republika Srpska Unit, the Special Police Unit, the Sekovici Unit, or the 1st PJP Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did you obtain or did you review the footage showing Kravica warehouse shortly after or possibly even during the tail-end of the massacre?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When did you say PJP stood for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The municipal police in the Zvornik area organised not only by local police stations, but when they were mobilised to do military functions they would be put into special municipal police units. We give them the acronym PJP. Those -- in the case of the 2nd Sekovici Detachment, it operated with one of those municipal police units, the 1st Municipal Police Unit. The police officers are made up from the Zvornik municipality or the whole sector for Zvornik. So that's -- it's a distinction that we make with respect to the members of the Special Police Brigade and those police officers who were there performing military-related duties who were normally police officers within the greater security sector of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 4559V on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, we're about to go to a segment of the film we just saw, which is a slow-motion segment, Petrovic Studio B footage. You've seen this before coming into court. Can you tell us the Studio B portion of the film depicting the Kravica warehouse, was that viewed or displayed in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that segment of the footage actually made it onto Belgrade TV with the original playing of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And in the -- at the time that footage was taken, we can hear voices in the vehicle, the people who were filming and talking amongst themselves. Do you know the identity of those persons?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them is Mr. Petrovic -- Pecanic, the other is Ljubisa Borovcanin. There's a third person in the vehicle, I don't know his identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if we could start this portion of the film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are these people media people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Petrovic is the media person. Ljubisa Borovcanin -- I'm sorry, Ljubisa Borovcanin is the commander or the deputy commander of the Special Police Brigade. The reason why Zoran Petrovic had the access that he had, was he spent a day accompanying Lieutenant-Colonel Borovcanin around on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Borovcanin, whose voice we hear in this film is the same one we saw of the individual who was standing next to the Serb -- VRS soldier with the blue helmet just a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now if we could play this segment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The segment we're watching, Mr. Butler, is the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In the upper right we can see the NTV logo. We did see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, if the Court wants to view that again, we can replay it. If not, I'll ask that it be given an exhibit number and admitted. It's a very short segment, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2400.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, now I'd like to turn to your report, if I can, again paragraphs 7.71 through 7.73 where you describe the -- and it's in Prosecution Exhibit 2264, where you describe the column and the events at that relate to it. Briefly, Mr. Butler, can you tell us approximately what percentage of the people in the column, from the original column that left Susnjari and Jaglici, how many of them actually arrived in Bosnian Muslim occupied territory, approximately?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the number -- and it's always kind of difficult because nobody really knows how big the column was to start with. I think the last number that I've seen on that may be about 4 or 5.000, maybe even as high as 7.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is that figure? Is that the figure of the people who originally left? Because the question is what percentage of that figure finally arrived.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The column size at its origin is estimated at approximately 12 to 15.000 people. I think somewhere between 5 and 7.000 ultimately arrive. So I guess we're looking at roughly half, maybe less.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, in paragraph 7.10 of P2246, you indicate that -- you indicate that people had been transferred -- transported, people who had been captured had been transported from the area of Bratunac and taken into the area of the Zvornik Brigade. Let me just ask you, the people who had been transported who would have been captured and been transport -- the males who had been transported to the area of the Zvornik Brigade, where were they transported to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were four primary locations that they were transported to. They were unused schools in the Zvornik Brigade area. One was the school at Grbavci. One was the school at Petkovci. The third was a school location at the village of Rocevic. The fourth one was a school at Pilica. And as the school at Pilica filled up, they ended up having to put people in the cultural centre in the village of Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the locations of those schools, in which brigade area of responsibility were those schools located?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are all within the area of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you've earlier identified Colonel Vinko Pandurevic as the commander of the Zvornik Brigade. Who was the deputy commander or chief of staff of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time that would be Major Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. If we could take a look at three documents in order -- if I could first of all have 65 ter 2591.06 on the monitor. Mr. Butler, let me ask you first of all, this document, as we can see on the left-hand side, upper left-hand side, this is from the commander of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade. This document is dated the 15th of July, 1995. It is an interim combat report to be delivered to the command of the Drina Corps. If we could turn, first of all, to see who the author of this document is. That would be to the next page we would see in the English translation the author of the document. Okay. This document has been authored by Colonel Vinko Pandurevic. I want to direct your attention to a portion that's on the first page. If we could return to the first page of the English. First of all, just in very general terms, Mr. Butler, what is this -- what does this report concern?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report is a report by the brigade commander personally to the Drina Corps explaining the current situation in his brigade zone with respect to a variety of activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could scroll up on the English version. Okay. And I want to direct your attention to the fourth paragraph from the bottom. It starts out with "An additional burden for us," and I can't see the complete English on that. So is there a way to view the complete English? Is looks like it's cut off a little bit. Okay. The passage, Mr. Butler, that says: "An additional burden for us is the large number of prisoners distributed throughout schools in the brigade area as well as obligations of security and sanitary technical measures in the field." To put this document in context, the 15th of July, 1995, what massacres had happened in the zone of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade by the 15th -- around the 15th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first of the large-scale executions started on the afternoon of the 14th of July at Orahovac. That continued to the late evening hours and approximately a thousand people were killed there. Following through in the late evening hours of the 14th through the early morning hours and almost until sunup on the 15th of July, another 800 to a thousand people who are held at the school at Petkovci are taken to the foot of an old dam and were executed there. Later on the day of the 15th the individuals who are being held at the school of Rocevic are taken to the bank of the Drina River in an area known as Kozluk and are executed at that location, and that is probably another 800 to a thousand. So as this interim report is being written, the prisoners held at the schools at Orahovac and ay Petkovci are already dead. And the ones that are being held at Rocevic are in the process of being killed on the banks of the Drina River at Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And at the same time this is happening, what is happening in respect of the column in the Zvornik Brigade area of operation?
