utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this juncture the Zvornik Brigade and the Drina Corps recognises the magnitude of the military threat that the column poses, and they are marshalling forces, either military forces or police forces, and trying to block the route of the column so it cannot escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you -- now, directing you to the portion I just read to you a minute ago, "An additional burden for us," can you comment on that particular portion. Particularly I'm interested in obligations of security and sanitary technical measures in the field. Can you comment on --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, my interpretation of this is what he's referring to is guarding the prisoners and the phrase "sanitary technicals" that's listed is here is "asanacija." I believe that reference is burying the prisoners after they've been executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Haven't we seen a document like this before?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour. I don't think this has yet been exhibited. I'm informed that this only is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a clear recollection of this report where the author was saying if he's not getting any assistance, he's going to let the people go.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That may be, Your Honour. That, I think, is another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is another document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2403.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, if I could just have a minute. I want to double check. Because that was the next document I was going to exhibit that I was -- wasn't informed that was already an exhibit. So if I can just have minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, you can exhibit it. I couldn't possibly tell you what exhibit number it is if it is, indeed, already admitted. So you might as well have it admitted. But I have that recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next document, then, that I'd like to show is 65 ter 2591.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, this document is a document that is dated the 16th of July, 1995, from the command of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. It is an interim combat report. We can go to the second page to see who the author is. Do you know who the author of this document was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's also the brigade commander, Colonel Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention, if I can, if we can scroll up on the English version to paragraph 3, and in this paragraph, Mr. Butler, it describes at the beginning of the paragraph, it describes the -- what is a -- clearly quite a difficult conflict that's taking place in the Zvornik area of responsibility, and then it says five lines from the bottom of that paragraph: "I have decided in view of the situation to open a corridor along the line of the three trenches for the civilian population - about 5.000 of them. I have agreed on a method of evacuation with the enemy side and this is now going forward." Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, based on the intensive combat that occurred with the column and the Zvornik Brigade and the forces in there, on the evening hours of the 15th and the early morning hours of the 16th, by the afternoon Colonel Pandurevic makes the decision on his own to conclude a 24-hour battlefield truce with the Bosnian Muslim forces to allow a chunk of this column to leave Bosnian Serb territory and make it over to Bosnian Muslim territory. In this particular interim combat report, that is what he's discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Could this be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2404.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could go to 65 ter 5754, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, let me identify this document first of all. This is a document that is from the command of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. It is dated the 18th of July, 1995. It's an interim combat report. Do you know who authored this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also Colonel Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of the English. I want to go to item number 4, to the bottom of the page. Mr. Butler, item number 4 says that: "During the last 10 days or so, the municipality of Zvornik has been swamped with Srebrenica Turks. It is inconceivable to me that someone brought in 3.000 Turks of military age and placed them in schools in the municipality, in addition to the 7.000 or so who have fled into the forests." I invite your comments on this, please, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a bit of contextual history behind this it particular paragraph in this particular report. Once the Main Staff of the VRS found out that Colonel Pandurevic had concluded this battlefield truce to essentially allow parts of this column to escape, they put together a commission of senior VRS officers to go to the Zvornik Infantry Brigade and to determine what exactly happened and potentially recommend back to the Main Staff what, if any, sanctions should be placed on Colonel Pandurevic. This entire report, when you read it, is Colonel Pandurevic's laid out defence of his actions as well as the defence of the combat burden the Zvornik Brigade has been incurring for the last several months. And it's directed to the commander of the Drina Corps, his superior, to explain his actions and the things that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could this, Your Honour, be given an exhibit number, this item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2405.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, briefly can you summarise the role of the Zvornik Brigade in the massacres, in the detention and the transportation of the prisoners in the Zvornik area of responsibility? You outline it in your report with detail, but just for the purposes of this record, can you summarise it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm try and do it as quick as possible. Zvornik Brigade personnel and equipment were used in part to transfer the captured men from in and around Bratunac to the Zvornik area. Zvornik Brigade soldiers were used to guard them at these facilities. Soldiers of the Zvornik Brigade participated in the Orahovac executions, as well as now the investigation has learned the Rocevic executions at Kozluk, engineers from the Zvornik Infantry Brigade and equipment from the Engineering Company was used to bury the bodies of these individuals. As other prisoners were taken other trucks were used to transport them. Many of these prisoners are subsequently still missing. So I mean in a nutshell, large components of all sections of the Zvornik Brigades had at least some role in these larger crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Butler. If we could turn to 65 ter 4559W.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This clip, Your Honours, is a clip depicting the survivors of the column as they walk through into the territory occupied by the Bosnian forces, Bosnian government forces. So if we could play that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: May this film clip, Your Honour, be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2406.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, I want to turn your attention to a different topic now. In part your report you focus on General Krstic and General Zivanovic and when General -- the time when General Krstic assumed command of the Drina Corps. I'm going to refer you to section 9.12 of Prosecution Exhibit 2246 and the ensuing paragraphs of that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 411 on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, the document that's on the monitor in front of you is a document that says in the upper left-hand corner, "Command, Drina Corps." It's dated the 13th of July, 1995, and the subject is "Handover of corps commander duties, information." I'd like to have you comment on this document, if you would, please.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is a document that was published by the chief of personnel and legal issues, Colonel -- or Lieutenant-Colonel Jovicic to the following units which are all of the subordinate units of the Drina Corps for the purpose of advising them that effective at -- on this date and this time that General Zivanovic was no longer the commander of the Drina Corps, and in fact that General Krstic was now assuming command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what does it say in respect of General Zivanovic and what his duties would be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was appointed to new duties within the VJ Army of Yugoslavia and VRS Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And below that paragraph, Mr. Butler, it refers to an individual, Colonel Svetozar Andric.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think we have seen Colonel Andric, Your Honours, in the film of the -- General Mladic entering into Srebrenica. He has been identified previously in that film.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again for purposes, Mr. Butler, of this document, tell us who Colonel Andric is and what position he assumed.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Andric was the commander of the 1st Birac Infantry Brigade of the Drina Corps. He was appointed as the chief of staff to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this document could be admitted into evidence and given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2407.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 5755 on the monitor, please. This document that we'll be referring to is referred to in paragraph 9.13 of Prosecution Exhibit 2246. It is specifically footnote 524.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, this is a document from the command of the Drina Corps. It is dated the 13th of July - and if we scroll up on the English version. Thank you - it is an order to search the terrain, and it is issued by commander Major-General Radislav Krstic. Can you comment on this document, please, and what significance it had, Mr. Butler, in terms of dating the time when General Krstic assumed command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is the first written order that the Office of the Prosecutor is aware of that General Krstic signed as the corps commander. We've actually in series of timing when you look at the outbound transition stamps, I believe this is approximately 2030 hours is when this was received by the communications centre -- or 2000 hours by the communications centre, and then dispatched 30 minutes later. So it serves to confirm the view that by approximately 2000 hours on 13 July 1995, General Krstic is functioning as the Drina Corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could this document, Your Honours, be given an Exhibit Number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2408.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And would that be a convenient time, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have two very, very brief questions, Your Honour. Yes, it will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Just in terms of General Krstic, did he have a nickname, and if you know, what was it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was often referred to by General Mladic and other generals as Krle.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And did General Zivanovic have a nickname, and if so -- if you know, what was it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again the same people referred to him as Zile.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. This is a convenient time, Your Honour, to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We will take a break and return at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, in your report P2246 paragraph 6.29, you mention that persons who had surrendered or were captured from the column were detained in multiple locations. We've already discussed the Sandici meadow. Where else besides the Sandici meadow were persons who were captured or who had surrendered from the column detained?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were detained at the football stadium in the town of Nova Kasaba, which was also the garrison of the 65th -- I am sorry, the military police battalion of the 65th Protection Regiment. They were held in the town of Konjevic Polje, that intersection down there, either under police or military control. There was a smaller group held in a meadow near Sandici called Jaglici. And those were the primary collection areas that we were aware of on 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So I see from the map that we've just introduced, which is P2400, that both Nova Kasaba and Konjevic Polje are indicated on the map. Let me just turn now to some exhibits, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have Prosecution Exhibit 274 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, this is referred to in your report in paragraph 12.8, Prosecution Exhibit 2246. Mr. Butler, the -- can you date this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This intercept is dated 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the two participants in the interview are identified as Beara and Lucic, and apparently a third person, Zoka, barely audible. Who is Beara?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beara is Colonel Ljubisa Beara. He is the chief of security on the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And can you identify Lucic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sorry. Could you identify Lucic? Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us the significance of this intercept, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular intercept, they are discussing locations and numbers of Bosnian Muslim prisoners that are being taken along various portions of the road on 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if we go in this intercept to the third portion where Beara or letter B is speaking -- I'm sorry. It appears to be the portion where it says B at the top: "Do you hear me? Do you know that 400 balijas have shown up in Konjevic Polje?" Can you comment on that, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, the investigation is aware that prisoners were being detained at Konjevic Polje. The discussion here is relative to the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Do you know what happened to those prisoners who had been detained at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number of different routes that they all took. Some of them ended up going later down to Sandici and ended up in the Kravica warehouse. Others were on buses and trucks. They spent the evening of 13 July, and some of them potentially the 14th of July, in Bratunac and then were later transferred to the area of the Zvornik Brigade and presumably died in the mass executions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we turn to Prosecution Exhibit 273, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, this intercept, in the third line down -- actually, let me invite your comments on this intercept. Mr. Butler, what is the significance of this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, first it talks about Malinic's unit in a location that they have 1.500 people gathered there at the stadium. The individual named Malinic is Major Zoran Malinic. He is the commander of the Military Police Battalion of the 65th Protection Regiment, and they are garrisoned at Nova Kasaba, and again to date this document is 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Malinic's unit, the 65th Protection Regiment, is a subordinate unit of which superior unit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 65th Protection Regiment is directly subordinate to the Main Staff of the army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you -- based on your review of the documents and the evidence, what role did the members of the 65th Protection Regiment have in the events that we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were active in combat against the column as it came over the road between Konjevic Polje and Nova Kasaba and were active in capturing prisoners at that location and holding them at the soccer field at Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did they have any additional role in dealing with the prisoners from Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they were suspected of being directly involved in some executions. However, since I have been out of the Tribunal for a number of years, I cannot tell you what the state of the investigation is with respect to them and whether they've ever been able to prove their involvement or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Could we turn to Prosecution Exhibit 266, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, are you able to date this intercept? This is referred to in your report, paragraph 7.64. It's footnote 452.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I believe we date this intercept -- I just want to be clear on it. I'm sorry, could you say the footnote again, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Footnote 452.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, 452. Yes, sir. This one is dated 14 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And the -- there's some features of this intercept I want you to explain to the Court. First of all, the first line -- actually, let me go up to the top. It says: "Participants, Palma Duty Officer (Major Jokic)" Who is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Jokic, Major Dragan Jokic is the chief of engineer services for the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. On 14 July 1995 he was also serving duty as the brigade duty officer at the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there's a reference in the intercept. We can see it in that same line where Major Jokic is identified. The reference is -- it says "Palma Duty Officer." Tell me what Palma is a reference to.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each of the units had a telephonic code-name that was associated with it. Palma was the telephonic code-name for the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. You'll see another one, Badem. Badem is the telephonic code-name for the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, where it -- at the top it says, "The Palma duty officer wants to talk to him. Beara is needed urgently ..." Again, can you identify Beara in this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, say again, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you identify the Beara who is referred to in this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is the same -- this is the same Colonel Beara from the Main Staff security administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if you go down below that it says: "The superior commander urgently needs him." What is the reference to superior command? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular context, the superior commander that they're talking to is the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The Main Staff of the VRS; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just -- can you comment on this intercept, Mr. Butler, and its significance?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, one of the things that we used this particular intercept for is that the knowledge of, one, the fact that they were aware where Beara is and people are trying to track him down and pass a message that they need to talk to him --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. I do hate to interrupt, but if we could have a little bit more specific language than "they," because he's saying there's some significance. So we'll just --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would be glad to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you be more precise, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you look at the text, "I'm the duty officer Palma. I need Beara urgently." So in this particular context, the "they" that are looking for them are the Zvornik Brigade. Keep in mind at this particular time there are probably upwards of 3.000 prisoners in various schools up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Up where? When you say up there --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Up where, being the Zvornik Brigade area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. And lieutenant -- Colonel Beara was heavily engaged in that effort. So ultimately what happens in this conversation is that Badem, Bratunac, puts him on the line and is discussing issues in this particular context talking about the column breaking through. "The Turks have pushed our guys back towards Crni Vrh," a location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And there's a reference in this intercept a little bit further down where it says: "We were together, Colonel, sir, number 155 called you and asked you to call him urgently." Based on your review of the documents, can you identify this -- what number 155 designates?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. On the military telecommunications network, the number 155 is the phone number that is for the operations room of the VRS Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we go down further in that intercept -- if we could scroll up, please in the English version. Okay. Bottom line of this intercept it says: "Yes, hey." "J" designates Jokic in this conversation. So Jokic says: "Yes, hey. We have huge problems over here." Could we go to the second page of the English. To the top of this document. And then at the top we see Jokic saying: "There are big problems. Well with the people, I mean, the parcel." Okay. What significance -- what is the significance of the term "parcel," Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a general awareness that the Bosnian Muslims had the ability and were intercepting these VRS telecommunications, these voice telecommunications on their multichannel network. So they often tried to talk around certain issues by using code words. One of the frequent euphemisms that we hear for people associated with being prisoners are parcels.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this -- contextually, Mr. Butler, this intercept takes place on the 14th of July, 1995. It's emanating from the Zvornik area. Put this in context for us, this intercept.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, at this particular point in time you have several events happening in the Zvornik Brigade area. On the criminal side you have the executions that are being finished up at the school at Orahovac. Further to the south and to the east in the area of Snagovo and in the hills to the south, the armed portion of the column has just broken through the VRS ambushes that were down in that area and are now moving towards the north, north-east -- I'm sorry, north, north-west and are in a position to threaten the rear areas now of several battalions of the Zvornik Brigade. So you see a series of intercepted telephone calls that go by reflecting the fact that their lines are being broken by the column coming up the south. They are dealing with all of these other issues. They're running out of manpower, and they are frantically calling for help.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Could we turn to Prosecution Exhibit 271 as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This, Mr. Butler, is in paragraph 10.23 of your report, footnote 583.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm just trying to locate the intercept in the right-hand side in the B/C/S version, because --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be the first line. "Colonel Beara looking for General Zivanovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So we have the same difficulty that we've discussed earlier, Your Honour. This intercept that's reproduced in English is -- the first -- the top lines of this larger text. We'll resolve that, Your Honour, with -- a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: But tell me, Mr. Butler, this is -- first of all, what is the date is this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has been dated to 15 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And can you identify the significance of this particular intercept in the context of the events that were taking place in the Zvornik area of responsibility -- or in the Drina Corps area of responsibility? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first of a series of related intercepts where Colonel Beara, who has now gone back to Zvornik, is looking for assistance from the Drina Corps to deal with issues related to the prisoners. As the text says, Colonel Beara looking for General Zivanovic. He's not there. He left -- "he" being Colonel Beara leaves the message for the general to call him at extension 139.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know who and what extension 139 was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Extension 139 is the phone in the office of Lieutenant Drago Nikolic, the chief of security for the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And on the 15th of July, can you contextualise what had happened in the Zvornik area of responsibility by -- at or approximately 9.52 hours in the morning when this intercept -- when this conversation was intercepted?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the one hand with the column, the column is still progressing to the north, north-west and is getting closer to the rear areas of several of the battalions of the Zvornik Brigade. On the criminal side, the prisoners at Orahovac are dead, but their engineers are still involved in burying them. They've just finished executing the last of the prisoners at the Petkovci dam. And they're now having to deal with all of the prisoners that are at the school in Rocevic as well as those further north in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next exhibit which is Prosecution Exhibit 272.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is found in your footnote 584 in Prosecution Exhibit 2246. This -- Mr. Butler, first of all, can you date this intercept for us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this is 15 July 1995, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this takes place -- this conversation is intercepted at 9.54, which is two minutes after the previous intercept we look at, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell us the significance of this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular intercept, Colonel Beara and General Zivanovic are talking about the issue of the reinforcements that were supposed to be sent up to the Zvornik Brigade to deal with some of these for whatever reason did not make it. And he's petitioning General Zivanovic to try and bring in more replacements to deal with these issues. I believe if you scroll further down, he's talking about send -- you know, have them, at least a platoon sent immediately. And at this particular juncture what you have is General Zivanovic saying, "I can't order that any more," a reflection that General Zivanovic is no longer the corps commander and does not have the authority to order various units of the Drina Corps to do things. And he gives him another extension number, 385.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what is that extension number?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, as it says further down, it says Zlatar and 385.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zlatar is a telephonic code for the Drina Corps, and 385 is an extension that's run out to the forward command post of the Drina Corps where General Radislav Krstic is at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Can we turn to the Prosecution Exhibit 264, please. This is found in paragraph 10.5 of Prosecution Exhibit 2246, and it is found in and referred to in footnotes 585 to 587.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This, Mr. Butler, is a conversation at 1000 hours. First of all, what date does this conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 15 July 1995, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the two participants are Colonel Ljubisa Beara and General Krstic. Now, can you explain the significance of this intercept to us, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Again, Colonel Beara now talking with General Krstic, asking for at least an additional 30 men, just like was ordered. Krstic is telling him take them from Nastic or Blagojevic. Nastic at this time is the commander of the Milici Brigade. Blagojevic is the commander of the Bratunac Brigade. And General Krstic, who is involved right now with the Zepa operation, is saying that, "I can't take any people out from here." Beara's basically saying is they don't have any people either, "And I can't do anything with -- without another 15, 30 men," and that they didn't arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we scroll down to the bottom of this -- up -- can we scroll up on the English version of the intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could continue, Mr. Butler, in describing in intercept.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Beara, as you can tell from the text, is -- is a little bit frustrated, says, "I don't know what to do any more." And of course General Krstic at that point suggests that you take some of the guys from the MUP, the police officers. And Beara's saying they won't do this. They won't do anything. "I've talked to them, and there's no other solution." Then goes down to the bottom and then finally you have Colonel Beara saying to General Krstic, you know, that I have still have 3.500 parcels that I have to distribute, and I have no solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And your interpretation of 3.500 parcels, Mr. Butler, in the context of -- first of all, tell us the context of 15 July in the area of the -- Zvornik and how you interpret 3.500 parcels.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, Colonel Beara is a security officer; he's not a combat commander. And given the military police situation, the fact that Colonel Pandurevic is now returning to the area, I -- I can only take this conversation that what they're referring to in 3.500 parcels is prisoners that are still located at the schools.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, was this conversation that we've looked at, P264, intercepted from multiple locations by the members of the Bosnian government army forces?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And you have recorded the various versions -- different versions of this in your report; is that correct, in footnotes 585 to 587?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I've highlighted the fact that various versions of this particular intercept exist and that there are slight linguistic differences in how they were transcribed as well as from one particular site, one of the correspondents was not necessarily, I believe, either faded out or could not be heard on a regular basis. So there are multiple versions of this particular intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All captured from different intercept locations; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Those, Your Honour, for the record, are Prosecution Exhibits 268, 267, and 238. Those other versions are identified in Mr. Butler's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to Prosecution Exhibit 269, Mr. Butler. This is found in your report, paragraph 1040. It's footnote 600, Mr. Butler. Can you -- Mr. Butler, can you date this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This particular intercept is dated 16 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this happens in the morning hours at 1111 hours. And the two participants are Colonel Beara and an individual identified as Cerovic. Who is Cerovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cerovic in this intercept is Colonel Slobodan Cerovic. He is the assistant commander for morale, legal, and religious affairs for the Drina Corps. On this particular day, he is functioning as the duty officer of the Drina Corps at the headquarters in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you interpret this intercept, please, in the context of the events and in the context of the other documents you've reviewed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular context, you have Colonel Beara talking to Colonel Cerovic, and they discuss the fact that triage needs to be done on the prisoners. In this sense at this particular time, they're not separating prisoners. So the euphemism "triage" in this particular case refers to killing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And again based on your review of the materials, can you enlighten us as to what happened on the 16th of July in respect of killings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the prisoners that were held at the school in Pilica were taken by buses and trucks to the Branjevo farm where they were executed, and once those executions were completed, the last sizable group of prisoners, those that were in the Pilica cultural centre in the town of Pilica were killed on the spot there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Butler. Could we turn to three intercepts that relate to Colonel Vujadin Popovic. Again we've seen Colonel Popovic, Mr. Butler, in various clips of film footage that we reviewed yesterday. Just again for purposes of this set of documents, who was he and what was his position?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Popovic was the Drina Corps assistant commander for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have Prosecution Exhibit 270 on the monitor, please. This is referred to, Mr. Butler, in paragraph 10.41 of your report. It's your report, Prosecution Exhibit 2246. I'll just confirm that for a minute. Tell me, first of all, Mr. Butler, can you interpret this intercept for us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It starts out as a conversation where these duty officers Zlatar and Palma are trying to get in touch with other. They do, and the Palma duty officer relays a message that 500 litres of diesel fuel are needed for Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic. The line of course disconnects and then it re-picks up again, and he can tell that they're looking; I need to speak to the Zlatar duty officer. Ultimately he gets connected to an individual named Basevic, who was an officer in the Drina Corps rear services division. And they're talking about, you know, the duty officer at Palma is talking about Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic needs 500 litres of fuel, or the work that he's doing is going to stop. Basevic responds back, "Don't you have that?" And the Palma duty officer says, "Well, I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page of the English translation, second page. I didn't ask you to date this intercept, Mr. Butler. Can you date this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This date is 16 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And on the second page of this, can you now review that and continue with your description of this.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the conversation cuts out and then they switch over to -- ask for Major Golic. Major Golic is a Drina Corps officer with the intelligence section of the Drina Corps who's at Vlasenica. So the duty officer is saying, you know, pop - that's his nickname for Popovic - Pop just called, told me to contact you. 500 litres of the fuel have to be sent immediately, otherwise his work will stop. Couple more switches, and then Palma, the duty officer, again says: "A bus loaded with oil is to go to Pilica village. That's it, 500 litres."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what work was going on, on the 16th of July, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pilica the work that was going on is that the buses who were taking the people who were held in the school, they were being transferred by buses from the school location to Branjevo farm where they were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic receive his 500 litres of fuel?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we take a look at 65 ter 2513, please. There are apparently two English translations. The ERN number on this is 00844508. Mr. Butler, can you orient us through this document, please, and what its significance is in relation to the previous intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is a document that originated from the technical services people of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade reflecting that 500 litres of diesel fuel had been dispersed to -- in the name of Colonel Popovic, and it's a remark at the bottom that 140 litres were subsequently returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay, now, on this document just for everybody's benefit, where does it says that it was disbursed to Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at line number 14 and line number 15. Command of the Drina Corps; and then 15, Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So those are the boxes that are designated by 14 and 15 on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2409.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now I'd like to take a look at some additional intercepts that relate to Colonel -- Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic. Could we have Prosecution Exhibit 276 on the monitor. This is referenced in paragraph 10.50 of your report that we've been referring to, Prosecution Exhibit 2246.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. That upside-down version isn't particularly helpful. There we go. Thank you. If we could scroll to the top of that English version. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, first of all -- well, let's wait to get it on the screen so it's in the right --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Only a portion of this is reproduced on the English version. Could it go into a lower font, smaller sized font? We still have the -- we need to get it in the right sized font. Just a minute. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, first of all, can you date this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This intercept has been dated 17 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And can you tell us who the correspondents are in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe "X" is ever identified, but "T" is Trbic. He is the deputy security officer for the Zvornik Brigade under Lieutenant Drago Nikolic. And on this particular day, Trbic is the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell us the significance of this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As referent X, or correspondent X, I guess, is the best way to say that, is looking for the location of Popovic, Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that referred to by the name Pop?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is a nickname that is often associated with Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indicating that Popovic is north of you, and then saying, they want -- "Leave right away for here for Zlatar 01."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is Zlatar 01?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zlatar is the code-name for the Drina Corps. When you see a number associated like that, 01, they're referring to the commander personally. So the phrase "Zlatar 01" refers to General Krstic at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And what's the significance of this intercept, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The north of here towards that task, geographically speaking, Pilica is to the north of the Zvornik Brigade headquarters. Reflecting a common knowledge of what that task is north of you. The other significance that I have always placed in this is part of the Krstic trial was the fact that how widespread the knowledge is to include, you know, General Krstic, Zlatar 01.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now can we look at Prosecution Exhibit 244 which is an intercept that takes place at 1249 hours. This is referred to in your report, paragraph 1050. Mr. Butler, can you, first of all, give us a date for this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been dated at 17 July 1995, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And is the correspondent Trbic the same individual you have identified just in the previous exhibit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Tell us the significance of this particular intercept.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular intercept, it's a reflection that the orders have now changed. The person that they were talking about, "Let him now finish the work. If you get in touch with him, let him finish that work and then have him come." And then there's another comment several lines later down that's basically says: "And have him report immediately here at Golac."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What does that mean, "at Golac"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If one takes the phrase they're referring to Golic and not Golac, that's would be report back to the Drina Corps headquarters where Major Golic is at the time. So he's basically instructing him that once the work is done to come back to the Drina Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Can we look at a related intercept, Mr. Butler. It's Prosecution Exhibit 245. This is referenced in paragraph 10.52 of your report, Prosecution Exhibit 2246. Mr. Butler, can you date this intercept, please?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, this intercept has also been dated 17 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you identify its significance in the events that relate to the crimes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the correspondents is inaudible. The other one is Popovic, Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic. He refers to one individual as "boss." In the context of the discussions that we here of these individuals, his superior, "boss," is in fact General Krstic. And he's reporting back, everything's okay, that the job is done. "It's all been brought to an end with no problems." He's noting the fact that he's at the base, wants to take a break and then, you know, he'll see you later. Or I think it says, he want to take a shower, and then, "I'll think again later. The job gets an A, a grade A. It's all taken care of."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What's your interpretation of the job as being referred to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Popovic was involved with the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see no indication of the intercept indicating there was a job.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Let me rephrase that then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is your interpretation of the word "basically that gets an A, an A, the grade A, everything's okay"? What's your interpretation of this intercept, Mr. Butler, and its significance in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, two things. Again if you look if he first line of the intercept it notes that the job is done. That job is, in fact, the completion of the burial. The last bodies were buried at Pilica on 17 July 1995. The fact that it gets an A, it's done, it's completed. Gets we finished all the work that we have to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Finally, Mr. Butler, I'd like to turn to what's referenced in chapter 11 of your report, paragraph 11. And we're going to be dealing with the subject of the reburials. First all, Mr. Butler, can you summarise what burials you're referring to in general terms and explain to the Trial Chamber when those took place and why they took place.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In the middle of August 1995, at the United Nations, a number of governments laid forth evidence of the mass executions that had occurred with respect to Srebrenica. And some of that evidence included aerial images of prisoners in various groups as well as burial operations afterwards. Once it was clear that a number of the sites where the bodies were identified and were known now to the international community, the VRS embarked on a roughly two-month effort to go into those sites in the evenings, disinter the remains of the executed prisoners and then to hide them further in the woods in, what we call, secondary or even tertiary grave sites, in far more remote locations in an effort to hide the evidence of the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 2610 on the monitor, please. Mr. Butler, this document is from the General Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska. It bears a number, 03/4-2341, and it is dated the 14th of September, 1995. It is urgent. It is addressed to the command of the Drina Corps logistics sector of the General Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska, with a copy to the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade for their information. And the name that appears at the bottom left of this document is the commander Colonel-General Ratko Mladic. Can you inform the Trial Chamber the significance of this particular document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is a document where General Mladic directs that five tons of diesel fuel be allocated and delivered to standard barracks in Zvornik. Standard is the former standard shoe factory which was the wartime headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade. It puts the fuel in the custody of Captain Milorad Trpic, a slight error. In fact, it's Milorad Trbic, who is the same deputy chief of security of the Drina Corps -- I'm sorry, deputy chief of security for the Zvornik Infantry Brigade that we discussed earlier. Notes that he's going to be responsible for the accurate maintenance of the records, the fuel use and the engine hours for this particular task. Completely interesting in so much as the fact that, again, Captain Trbic is a security officer; he's not an engineer. So that is why this message is generally and specifically interpreted by me to be related to the reburial operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this Exhibit be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2410.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn to a related item, Mr. Butler. Could we have 65 ter 2611 on the monitor, please. Mr. Butler, this is a 14 September 1991 document emanating from the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska logistical sector technical division. It is urgent. It is directed to the command of the 35th logistics base, the Drina Corps command for information, and the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade for information. It is signed by Colonel Zarko Ljubojecic. Can you tell us the significance of this document in particular in relation to the previous document that we examined, Prosecution Exhibit 2410?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. As you can see in this particular document it notes pursuant to the order of the commander of the Main Staff, and then later in the document references that order, directs the 35th logistics base to issue 5.000 litres of diesel fuel. It further notes that a Drina Corps representative shall collect the fuel and provide the transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In this document, what is it associated with, Mr. Butler, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a follow-on disbursal order for the Main Staff for the fuel related to the burial operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have concluded my examination of Mr. Butler, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, may I have just a moment. I failed to seek an exhibit number on the last document, Your Honour, 65 ter 2611. If that could be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2411.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While we're waiting for Mr. Guy-Smith, can I just ask one question, Mr. Butler. Were the secondary or even tertiary burial places all identified and found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. As a component of the investigation, and I can't give you the number off the top of my head, sir, but I believe there are in the neighbourhood of 30 of them that have been identified over the years. Almost all of them have been exhumed to this juncture. There may be others out there that have yet to be identified, but I believe that most of them have been identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry about that, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not a problem. Not a problem at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good evening, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I know you've testified many times. I know you've testified for many days. I do not intend on keeping you here for one of those long bouts that you've been in before. However, I'm sure we're going to spend some time with each other. I'm saying that to give you some kind of hope.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've learned to dispel all hope when I come in here, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to -- I'd like to start if I could just very briefly with regard to an understanding of the cases in which you've testified. You've mentioned a number of those cases. And in addition it's my understanding that you've testified, I believe at least twice in the United States District Court on immigration, or what I believe to be, as I understand them, extradition matters. One in the case of United States v. Veselin Vidacak, case number 1-06CR278-1, which was in Greensboro, North Carolina; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you also testified, I believe, in the case of United States v. Marko Baskic, CR-04-10298-DPW, and that I believe was in Massachusetts.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I may have missed one, I think, there was actually one other one, too, which was the case of Milovic and Jankovic, which was also a Greensboro case, case number 1:05CR277; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I may have --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]...

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are additional cases that I have testified in, but those are the early three or four, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say there are additional cases you've testified in, are you referring to additional cases that you've testified in, in the United States court system with regard to issues concerning, what I will call, in a general sense, the conflict?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And before we go any further, could you just identify those cases for us if -- if you can?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a series of three or four cases out of the Middle District of Florida. I believe it would be the United States Government v. Popovic, United States Government v. Krsmanovic. There is one more whose name of the defendant escapes me. There was an additional criminal case in Cleveland. So I guess that's Northern District of Ohio. US v. -- what's the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We'll get to it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from that, I believe you've also testified in some special war crimes tribunals; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I've been asked to and I've testified in Srebrenica-related cases before the special -- or the state war crimes court in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm just trying to get it -- just a rough idea. It's fair to say that you have been occupied with the matters concerning Srebrenica clearly for over a decade; true?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in that -- in that regard, you've -- you have had occasion to, from what I understand, both here as well as in other testimonies, you've had occasion to review thousands of documents, videotapes, books, studies; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, just to keep in mind that my period of daily active work with this material ended in November of 2003, although I've had periods where I have been able to come back here to The Hague and spend several weeks or a month looking at new material in preparation for the subsequent trials.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand that. And with regard, just so we have a general understanding, apart from documents that you've looked at which you've discussed with us here today, and by that I mean documents that were seized from one particular army, by that I mean the VRS, as I understand it you've also had occasion to review, as you told us the other day, the Dutch report on Srebrenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Dutch report that I reviewed on Srebrenica was the initial Dutch debriefing report that was done in 1995. I have not reviewed the Dutch Nijad [phoen] report is, I think, the one that you're referring to. That was actually being published, I believe during the Blagojevic trial. So I've never spoken to the individuals associated with that, and I have not reviewed that report in any detail. I'm not even sure which parts of it have been translated into English yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to the case of General Krstic, this is a case that you actively worked on, as you've told us both during the trial phase and during the appeal phase, if I understood your testimony correctly.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And with regard to your work in that case, did you -- did you have occasion to review the testimonies of such individuals as Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have read his -- his statements. I don't recall that I would have followed his court testimony, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I just have a first name for Halilovic? Which Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Enver. That's Hadzihasanovic. It's Enver. Sefer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The day has gone by -- the day is long. Sefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you like a break, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I'll go for the ten minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, I probably read his statement. I don't know that I followed his court testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I want to take -- what I want to do is just take a moment here with regard to your familiarising yourself with the Bosnian Muslim army individuals, if I could.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell the Chamber who Enver Halilovic [sic] was during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that General Halilovic was at one point one of the senior commanders of the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just so that we don't get confused a little later, now Halilovic at line 13 is given the first name Enver. We had corrected that to Sefer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And with regard to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I'm saying this because subsequently, the correction now is being -- we got it wrong again on the script.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh, dear. Thank you so much, Your Honour. If we could have a correction on line --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if you don't mind just while we're dealing with the Bosnian Muslim army, if you don't mind calling it the Bosnian Muslim army or the ABiH, just so that we don't run into problems later on.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Did you become acquainted with a gentleman by the last name of Delic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know generally of him. I don't know many of the details related to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Generally, when you know say generally, could you put him in the pantheon of the Bosnian Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think maybe you should give us the first name of this Delic, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm so bad on first names. Rasim. Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It's been a few years. Rasim Delic is also a senior general with the Bosnian Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And a name that I'm going to mispronounce, which is Enver Hadzihasanovic. Are you familiar with -- with that particular individual in terms of being a part of the Bosnian Muslim army during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Again, I don't recall his exact position, but I am aware that he was a -- a general, and again in the senior leadership positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to your work in the Krstic case, did you have occasion -- as you sit here today, did you have occasion -- I guess, first of all, I have to ask if you remember reviewing any of their testimonies with regard to the prosecution of General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. If I recall the timing correctly, they were after at least the initial trial of General Krstic. So again -- I know that certainly in the case of Mr. Hadzihasanovic, I believe, and Delic, that they were the subject of proceedings here, but I think that those came in time, after General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate that. What I'm referring to is having -- whether or not you had occasion to review their testimonies as against General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, as against General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with regard to the analysis, and I'm now dealing with it in the most general of terms first of all. With regard to the analysis that you were engaged in, I take it that part of what you had to sort through was the fact that at the time there were allegations of criminal activities there was also actual combat occurring; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And you've given us -- you've given us some help in that regard by mentioning, if I'm not mistaken, that's the 28th Brigade, which was the Bosnian Muslim brigade.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the 28th Infantry Division, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And with regard to the 28th Infantry Division, during the period of time that your testimony is focussed on that in July, could you tell us who was the commander of the 28th Infantry Division for the Bosnian Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The nominal commander would have been Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say nominal commander, what is the particular use of that adjective in your response?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May of 1995, Naser Oric and a group of the other officers, senior officers from the 28th Infantry Division -- I almost hate to open this can of worms again, but basically were flown out of the enclave and were in Tuzla. So many of the senior officials from the 28th Infantry Division were not with the division at the beginning of Operation Krivaja 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And we'll be in this can of worms at some point or another, and I think that Mr. Harmon has earlier indicated today that there are other documents that are going to come in. This has become somewhat of a live issue in this case. To the extent that you've been getting the lash of anything, I do apologise, but such is life.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Occupational hazard, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Indeed so. With regard to them being flown out, you mentioned Oric. Who else was flown out, if you know, at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this was again based on the researches you've done and the documents that you've reviewed.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware that it was a number of senior commanders. I don't know the names of those individuals off the top of my head, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And after Naser Oric departed from the area, do you know who took over in his place instead?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I have in my report, if you will allow me to reference back --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you refer to your report, I take it you're referring to 2466, your narrative report; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, the revised narrative. I have some of the 28th Division materials, but I don't believe I mentioned the name of the commander in this particular passage, so I'll have to say at this juncture I don't recall who it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And finally just one last question for this evening but not one last question in this area. During the course of your research with regard to the Bosnian Muslim army, did you become aware of the fact that there were Mujahedin fighters who were in that army?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the entirety of the army, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Did you learn anything with regard to any of the benefits that the Mujahedin fighters received as a result of being involved with the Bosnian Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that those individuals were provided citizenship and were allowed to reside in Bosnia-Herzegovina after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And since I've used the term generically, "Mujahedin fighters," did you, in the documents that you reviewed and research that you did, obtain information from where these fighters came, and by that I mean by country or region or both?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The phrase "Mujahedin fighters" is associated with individuals who are not native from the region but are, in fact, individuals who, either from Arabic or other Muslim countries in north Africa, the Middle East, or south-east Asia, which fought with the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Would this be an appropriate time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, it is. We will take a break and come back tomorrow, this time at 9.00 in the morning, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is in courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Once again you are warned not to communicate with anybody during the break until you are excused from testifying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Court is adjourns to tomorrow -- THE USHER: [Overlapping speakers]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
